title: Refactor Contrived Failure Injection Playbook - Onboarding & Regression Collection
content:
Purpose
-----
Short: provide a compact, actionable collection of prompts and contrived failure cases for onboarding new code-gen/refactor models and catching regressions that only show up under subtle test or compile constraints. This is intended to be a smaller, focused complement to the larger corpora in applied-ml (not a replacement).

Why this exists
---
- Observed gaps: models that look fine on simple rewrite tasks still generate code that fails to compile, violates unit-level contracts, or subtly changes semantics under style constraints.
- Need fast, reproducible cases that exercise: compile errors, test flakiness, assertion-level semantics, and style-guided rewrites.
- Useful both for model onboarding (quick signal) and nightly regression checks.

Dataset composition (high level)
---
- ~120 prompt items, split across three buckets: 1) compilation-trigger prompts (40), 2) test-driven refactor prompts (45), 3) style-constraint and lint-preservation prompts (35).
- Each item includes: short prompt, minimal input repo snippet (<=150 LOC), expected behaviour (compile success / failing test name / style violations), and a short oracle hint for graders (human or automated).
- Lightweight human labels: severity (blocker/non-blocker), scenario tags, and a one-sentence rationale for the failure injection.

Use cases & workflows
---
- Quick onboarding: run the 15-minute smoke batch to get compile+unit pass rate across candidate model variants.
- CI regression: nightly job runs full playbook; regression alert if compile-rate delta > 3% or unit-pass delta > 5% against baseline.
- A/B rollouts: use the playbook as the gold prompt-set for canary checks (if canary fails > threshold, auto-fallback).

How items were created (notes)
---
- Seeded from real customer bug reports (anonymized): off-by-one in refactor, missing import after extraction, broken async/await conversion.
- Augmented by engineers with contrived failure injection: remove type annotations, add shadowed variables, swap equality operators.
- Goal: keep prompts realistic (not puzzles) — mimic transforms ML models perform in production.

Prompt templates (representative)
---
1) Compilation-trigger (example)\Prompt: "Refactor the helper module to extract a pure function for computing the checksum and replace in-place mutations with the new function. Ensure the module still imports properly."\Input snippet:
"""
# file: checksum.py
def compute(data):
    s = 0
    for i in range(len(data)):
        s += data[i]  # originally ints, sometimes bytes
    return s

# used in other modules: from checksum import compute_checksum"""
Expected behaviour: model must rename consistently (no broken import usage). Typical failure mode: model renames function but does not update callers -> ImportError or NameError.
Oracle hint: check for broken exports and missing symbol updates.

2) Test-driven refactor (example)\Prompt: "Simplify this class by extracting a validation method and add unit tests that assert the old behaviour remains unchanged."\Input snippet:
"""
# file: user_validator.py
class UserValidator:
    def validate(self, user):
        if user.email is None:
            return False
        if '@' not in user.email:
            return False
        if user.age < 0:
            return False
        return True

# unit tests assume exact ordering of checks to generate specific error codes"""
Expected behaviour: refactor must preserve control flow or tests must be updated in a compatible way. Failure mode: reordering checks changes error code semantics -> unit test failure.
Oracle hint: run unit tests that assert error codes and ordering.

3) Style-constraint / lint preservation (example)\Prompt: "Refactor to use list comprehensions and keep Pylint score >= 9.0. Preserve variable names used by external config files."\Input snippet:
"""
# file: transforms.py
def build_list(items):
    out = []
    for x in items:
        if x is not None:
            out.append(transform(x))
    return out"""
Expected behaviour: functionally equal rewrite, lint warnings limited to non-critical rules. Failure mode: rename of externally-referenced symbol -> downstream break.
Oracle hint: run pylint and check for symbol renames referenced in config.yaml.

Automated grading strategy
---
- Pipeline steps per item: (1) run model to produce patch / file rewrite (2) apply patch to minimal repo clone (3) build/compile (python -m py_compile / javac / go build as appropriate) (4) run targeted unit tests (pytest -q) (5) static analysis (pylint / golangci-lint) (6) semantic diff check (AST-level differences for critical functions).
- Grader outputs as short tags: compile_ok | compile_error | tests_pass | tests_fail | lint_ok | lint_fail | semantic_regress | import_broken.
- For flaky tests, we repeat the run 3x; if non-deterministic, escalate to human triage.

Metrics & thresholds (suggested)
---
- Compile rate: percent of items that compile after patch. Baseline target for onboarding: >= 92% for candidate models.
- Unit pass rate: percent of targeted tests passing. Baseline: >= 88%.
- Style compliance: median lint score drop <= 0.5 points.
- Semantic regression: flagged if any AST-level assertion shows changed control flow for critical functions.
- Alerting: nightly failure if compile_rate_delta > 3 pct points OR unit_pass_rate_delta > 5 pct points vs baseline model.

Failure injection taxonomy (short)
---
- Missing symbol updates (imports/call sites)
- Type/annotation removal causing runtime mismatch
- Control-flow reorder (affects error codes)
- Async/await mis-conversion (forgetting await)
- Shadowed variables or renamed constants referenced in config
- Test-level contract changes (assertion semantics altered)

Operational notes & quick run
---
- Quick smoke: run the "smoke15" batch which selects 15 high-signal items (5 from each bucket). Estimated run time: 10-15 minutes on CI runner with 2 containers.
- Full run: run complete playbook (approx 90-120 minutes depending on language variety).
- CI integration: see linked_artifacts PR for example job definitions. Use labels: eval/refactor-playbook/nightly.

Human review guidelines
---
- If grader tags include semantic_regress or import_broken, escalate to eng-applied-ml with priority: P1 if blocker severity.
- Human review checklist: reproduce locally, trace AST diff, check external reference map (config, callers), and write a one-paragraph summary.

Open TODOs (notes to self)
---
- [ ] Add 8 JS async/await contrived cases (Samira)
- [ ] Formalize AST assertion tooling for Java (Marco)
- [ ] Add CI badge integration and auto-alert Slack channel (EPIC JIRA-ENG-3201)
- [ ] Collate human review examples into Confluence page for triage runbooks

Appendix: short item index (examples)
---
- ITEM-013: missing-import-after-extract (python) — prompt asks to extract helper and leave public API surface intact. Expected failure: ImportError.
- ITEM-029: reorder-guard-conditions (python) — tests sensitive to order. Expected failure: tests_fail on test_error_codes.py::test_invalid_email_code.
- ITEM-047: await-dropped-in-refactor (javascript/ts) — expected failure: runtime UnhandledPromiseRejection.
- ITEM-078: rename-config-referenced-const (go) — expected failure: runtime config lookup nil.

Notes: keep items short, reproducible, and self-contained. The goal is not to stress models with massive repos; we want focused checks that map to real customer pain.

If you run this, please add results to confluence:Onboarding-Evals-Index and file a ticket with labels eval:refactor/regression.

End of playbook notes.
